notes: Grab (motorbike or car) is cheap and safe; a motorbike taxi costs 30,000-60,000 VND. Metro Line 1 (Ben Thanh-Suoi Tien) is open.
June to September is the rainy season: afternoon downpours are common, so sightsee in the morning and take an umbrella. Expect 32°C and humidity.
Pho costs 60-90,000 VND, banh mi 30-60,000, coffee 30-60,000. Street stools are safe, and the ice is factory-made.
For Cu Chi and the Mekong, a tour (hotel pickup included) is the most practical option. The Ben Duoc tunnels are quieter than Ben Dinh.
Cross the road at a steady pace (motorbikes will swerve around you). To avoid bag snatchers, don't hold your phone in your hand on the street.
Tipping is not expected; haggle 30-50% off at markets.

stops.name: War Remnants Museum
stops.tips: A museum of the Vietnam War: heavy but important. Cooler in the morning.

stops.name: Independence Palace
stops.tips: The palace tanks crashed into in 1975, with 1960s architecture and a bunker.

stops.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Saigon
stops.tips: The French cathedral (under restoration), with the Central Post Office opposite.

stops.name: Pho Hoa Pasteur
stops.tips: A classic spot serving pho since 1968, on Pasteur Street.

stops.name: Ben Thanh Market
stops.tips: The city's iconic market: coffee, dried mango, and haggling is a must.

backups.name: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa
backups.tips: Saigon's most famous banh mi, with 10 kinds of meat and a long queue.

backups.name: Saigon Central Post Office
backups.tips: A post office designed by Eiffel; step inside to see it.

stops.name: Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Duoc
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~500,000 VND, or bus number 13); a 200 km tunnel network. Ben Duoc is less touristy, with 20-100 m crawls.

stops.name: Cu Chi Tapioca Tasting
stops.tips: War-era tapioca and tea at the tunnel exit; included in the tour.

stops.name: Cu Chi Local Eatery
stops.tips: Eat com tam (broken rice) on the way back.

stops.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
stops.tips: Saigon's most atmospheric temple, with a turtle pond and incense.

stops.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
stops.tips: A pedestrian boulevard in front of the City Hall; cafes in the Cafe Apartment building (42 Nguyen Hue).

backups.name: Cafe Apartment Saigon
backups.tips: A 9-storey apartment block full of cafes; balcony views.

backups.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum
backups.tips: City history; an alternative to the pagoda.

stops.name: Binh Tay Market
stops.tips: Cho Lon's wholesale market; lively in the morning, with street breakfast.

stops.name: Thien Hau Temple
stops.tips: A temple to the sea goddess, with hanging spiral incense.

stops.name: Cho Lon Street Food Tour
stops.tips: Hu tieu (Cho Lon noodles) and dim sum on Ha Ton Quyen street.

stops.name: Cha Tam Church
stops.tips: The church where Diem was captured, in Cho Lon.

stops.name: Bui Vien Walking Street
stops.tips: The backpacker street: plastic stools, beer and noise.

backups.name: Com Tam Ba Ghien
backups.tips: The city's most famous com tam, in Phu Nhuan.

backups.name: Saigon Opera House
backups.tips: The A O Show bamboo circus; an alternative to Bui Vien.

stops.name: Tan Dinh Church
stops.tips: A pink-painted cathedral, ideal for photos.

stops.name: Tan Dinh Market
stops.tips: A local market; banh cuon for breakfast.

stops.name: Cong Caphe
stops.tips: Coconut coffee at Cong Caphe, plus egg coffee.

stops.name: Turtle Lake
stops.tips: The Turtle Lake roundabout: young crowds and street snacks.

stops.name: Secret Garden Restaurant Saigon
stops.tips: Vietnamese home cooking in a rooftop garden, in District 1.

backups.name: Banh Xeo 46A
backups.tips: Vietnamese savoury pancakes on Dinh Cong Trang.

backups.name: Fine Arts Museum Saigon
backups.tips: Art in a colonial mansion; an alternative to coffee.

stops.name: Vinh Trang Pagoda
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~600,000 VND, lunch included); giant Buddhas.

stops.name: Mekong River Boat Tour
stops.tips: A boat on the main river, with Unicorn Island and honey and coconut candy workshops.

stops.name: Ben Tre Canoe Tour
stops.tips: A sampan through palm-lined canals; included in the tour.

stops.name: Mekong Island Restaurant
stops.tips: Elephant ear fish and rice paper; included in the tour.

stops.name: Ben Tre Coconut Workshop
stops.tips: Coconut candy and souvenirs.

backups.name: Cai Be Floating Market
backups.tips: A morning floating market; an alternative to My Tho (early start).

backups.name: My Tho Hu Tieu Restaurant
backups.tips: My Tho noodles; an alternative to the island.

stops.name: Bitexco Saigon Skydeck
stops.tips: Views from the 49th floor; visibility is clear in the morning.

stops.name: Ho Thi Ky Flower Market
stops.tips: A flower market with Cambodian street food, in District 10.

stops.name: Ho Thi Ky Cambodian Noodles
stops.tips: Num banh chok, inside the market.

stops.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
stops.tips: Vietnam's tallest building, in Binh Thanh.

stops.name: Thu Thiem Riverfront
stops.tips: The city skyline at sunset from the new bridge; cafes.

backups.name: Saigon Waterbus
backups.tips: The river bus from Bach Dang; a cheaper alternative to Landmark.

stops.name: Tao Dan Park
stops.tips: Morning tai chi and birdcage coffee: the city's ritual.

stops.name: Pho Le
stops.tips: Sweet-style pho in District 5; a farewell breakfast.

stops.name: Saigon Square
stops.tips: Affordable clothing and souvenirs; air-conditioned.

stops.name: L'Usine Le Loi
stops.tips: A cafe-boutique with coffee and pastries; a farewell stop.

stops.name: Tan Son Nhat Airport Bus 109
stops.tips: 30 minutes to the airport by bus; farewell.

backups.name: Banh Mi 37 Nguyen Trai
backups.tips: Banh mi with grilled meatballs, from a street cart.

backups.name: Saigon Botanical Garden
backups.tips: A botanical garden and zoo; an alternative to the park.
